title: Splunk, SolarWinds Release Fresh Security Updates
description: Splunk and SolarWinds released security updates addressing multiple vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to execute code, escalate privileges, cause denial-of-service, and leak sensitive information. Splunk patched critical improper access control and data exposure issues in Splunk Enterprise and SOAR, while SolarWinds fixed a high-severity broken authorization flaw in Observability and medium-severity XSS, SSRF, and information disclosure bugs. These updates resolve dozens of security defects across product code and third-party libraries.
aiSummary: Splunk released security updates for Splunk Enterprise versions 9.4.16, 10.0.11, 10.2.8, and 10.4.4 addressing 16 CVEs including critical improper access control and neutralization issues (e.g., CVE-2026-76299, CVE-2026-76302). Splunk SOAR version 8.7.0 patches 15 vulnerabilities including critical data exposure and access control flaws (CVE-2026-76531, CVE-2026-76407). SolarWinds patched a high-severity broken authorization schema vulnerability in Observability (CVE-2026-28328) and medium-severity XSS, SSRF, and information disclosure bugs in Observability Self-Hosted 2026.4 and Patch Manager 2026.4. These updates collectively mitigate risks of remote code execution, privilege escalation, denial-of-service, and sensitive data leakage.
aiImpact: If unpatched, these vulnerabilities could allow attackers to execute arbitrary code, escalate privileges, bypass authorization controls, cause denial-of-service conditions, and access or leak sensitive information. The flaws affect core product functionality and third-party components, increasing the attack surface. Successful exploitation could compromise confidentiality, integrity, and availability of affected systems.
